statement: The turn loop assembles context, supports a separate Codex app-server turn path, then iterates preflight, request/retry, normalized tool-or-text response and finalization phases.
limits: Static call-path trace; provider success, cancellation timing and all early-return paths were not exercised.

statement: A model tool-call turn is persisted before dispatch; failed canonical persistence ends the turn before side effects.
limits: Persist-before-dispatch is not atomicity between a remote side effect and its later result receipt; no exactly-once external-effect claim.

statement: Session turn leases use a 300 second TTL, a default 60 second refresh interval, and separate liveness activity checks.
limits: A lease is concurrency ownership, not proof a model/tool is making useful progress; alternate configured timings may apply.

statement: Provider response-normalization transports are registry-based, discovering Anthropic, Codex, chat-completions and Bedrock modules; registered plugin API modes can be recognized.
limits: Normalization registry is only one part of execution; Codex app-server has its separate turn implementation; not every backend audited.

statement: Provider runtime documentation describes one shared resolver across CLI, gateway, cron, ACP and auxiliary calls, with explicit requests before saved config, environment and defaults.
limits: High-level documentation precedence; all credential refresh/fallback/custom-endpoint branches were not individually traced.

statement: System prompt construction orders stable, context and volatile tiers; skill index and memory occupy the volatile tier while pinned auto-loaded skill bodies enter stable prefix.
limits: Volatile means likely to change at rebuild, not rewritten every API request; the concrete ordering controls over contradictory guide prose.

statement: Built-in memory and external provider system blocks are assembled together; exposure of external provider tools gates its advertised block.
limits: No claim that this scans or semantically validates every provider's retrieved fact.

statement: Project context character cap defaults dynamically to 6% of model window times a character estimate, clamped from 20,000 to 500,000 characters; explicit config overrides.
limits: Characters are not exact tokens; caps are context-file limits, not the entire request or the subdirectory hint cap.

statement: Context-file truncation preserves 70% head and 20% tail plus a marker, with warnings and a path for reading omitted content.
limits: A retained heading or marker does not preserve omitted instruction semantics; warning does not guarantee later reread.

statement: Memory prompt invalidation at compression clears cached state and reloads snapshots for a rebuild boundary.
limits: Inspect the full function for other cache fields; mutation is not a refresh on every memory write.

statement: Anthropic cache planning is copy-on-write and supports a native tool-array breakpoint plus static prefix and two completed-transaction endpoints, or a maximum-four-marker message layout.
limits: Provider-specific optimization; markers do not promise cache hits or measured savings, and other providers use other semantics.

statement: Usage anchors capture provider prompt/completion counts plus transcript fingerprints, including the whole priced prefix, and estimate only appended-message deltas.
limits: Not a vendor tokenizer or full request fingerprint: external tool definitions and separately assembled system prompt are not independently fingerprinted here.

statement: Compression config base defaults: threshold .50, target ratio .20, protect first 3, recent count 20, max attempts 3 capped at10, in-place true, micro-compaction false.
limits: Effective trigger is adjusted by model overrides, output reservation, small-window floor and optional caps; recent count is opportunistic against token ceilings.

statement: For context windows below512,000, built-in compression raises threshold ratio to at least .75; effective input subtracts output reservation, with minimum-floor and .85 guard behavior.
limits: No universal .50 trigger. Explicit absolute/auxiliary caps can lower final threshold; model-specific auto-raise may raise ratio.

statement: Lean verbatim tail uses 2.5% of context clamped by lean floor/cap constants; legacy uses threshold times summary target ratio.
limits: Tail selection must preserve coherent tool groups/user anchors and may adjust actual retained size; not a fixed count of turns.

statement: Compression pipeline prunes a copied tool-result history, finds a compression window and summary path, then assembles the compressed transcript.
limits: Lossy compaction: preservation of full archived transcript does not make the model-visible summary lossless.

statement: Overflow recovery tracks bounded compression attempts; provider-proven overflow requests a cooldown-bypassing pass and distinguishes transient lock refusal from exhaustion.
limits: HTTP payload bytes and context tokens are different error classes. This is not proof every provider's error string is classified correctly.

statement: Context-engine API separates destructive/persisted compression from request-only select_context replacement and best-effort on_turn_complete observation.
limits: Custom engines may change cache prefix and have optional hooks; terminal failures can skip on_turn_complete.

statement: Memory config defaults enable two built-in stores, cap them at2200 and1375 characters, leave write approval off, nudge interval10 and no external provider selected.
limits: Character limits are not measured token guarantees; existing user config/migrations can differ. These defaults do not imply permission for this project to auto-write research memory.

statement: MemoryStore loads a frozen system-prompt snapshot; writes mutate disk state separately; strict threat scanning can substitute blocked-entry placeholders in the snapshot.
limits: Pattern scanning is a heuristic, not proof a memory is true/safe; preexisting oversized files are warned and loaded, not silently clipped.

statement: Memory mutations lock a separate lockfile, reread current disk state, detect destructive-edit drift and atomically write updated entries.
limits: Protects supported cooperating file writers; external manual edits can still create drift. Approval behavior and remote provider stores are separate.

statement: Memory prompt rendering returns the frozen load snapshot; disk writes use atomic_write_text and preserve foreign-content drift backups.
limits: Atomic local file replacement does not provide a multi-store or cross-service distributed transaction.

statement: Agent initialization loads built-in memory unless skipped or safe-worker gated, and optionally loads one configured external provider alongside it.
limits: An explicitly requested memory toolset can still load the built-in store when skip_memory is true; safe-worker and disabled-toolset gates matter.

statement: MemoryManager rejects a second external provider, protects reserved core tool names and snapshots recall spill policy when registering.
limits: The orchestrator's list-shaped API is not proof unlimited simultaneous external stores are supported.

statement: External prefetch runs on a context-propagating daemon thread with bounded wait; a stuck provider is skipped on later turns until it returns.
limits: Timeout does not forcibly terminate Python thread or undo remote work. No unbounded new thread per later turn for the same stuck provider.

statement: Turn start prefetch uses semantic user text, skips trivial prompts, notifies turn author and emits a deterministic recall indicator when context is injected.
limits: Whether recall was relevant/correct still depends on provider and task; image-only text may be trivial.

statement: Injected user context is stamped into api_content sidecar for exact replay while clean transcript content can remain separately stored.
limits: Sidecar semantics require the matching persistence path; this is not an assertion that no sensitive content is stored.

statement: Provider sync_turn sends redacted turn text and optional transcript through one serialized background worker, preserving ordering and bounded user-facing completion.
limits: Redaction patterns do not guarantee removal of all sensitive information. Queue completion and remote durability need explicit flush/provider semantics.

statement: Checkpoint-required pre-compress mode requires a capable provider to succeed or raises so caller can retain uncompressed transcript.
limits: Opt-in checkpoint contract, not universal default or transactional proof of every provider's storage.

statement: Current session_search returns actual stored messages with discovery/read/scroll/browse modes and makes no LLM calls.
limits: Built-in tool only; external memory providers can call models. Search ranking does not establish factual correctness.

statement: Search hides kanban/subagent/tool sources, demotes cron matches, caps raw discovery scan300, read-message content2000 and exclusion IDs20.
limits: These are implementation defaults at pin, not complete semantic recall guarantees; hidden sources are not deleted.

statement: SessionDB search uses FTS with canonical-row fallback routes for stale/corrupt indexes, including CJK/trigram handling.
limits: Runtime indexing availability/platform extension behavior was not executed; not default vector search.

statement: State schema includes canonical messages, model usage, runtime epoch, durable session admissions, managed-worker executions and receipts.
limits: Schema existence alone does not prove every legacy writer goes through all revision fences.

statement: Started admissions/workers from a prior owner epoch become unknown; started external effects are not blindly replayed.
limits: Unknown requires reconciliation. This sacrifices automatic liveness rather than claiming exactly-once external actions.

statement: Claiming new input refuses while unknown input or worker execution blocks the session.
limits: Core admission store path only; all other platform delivery semantics are not thereby proven.

statement: Managed compression mutates archive/publication and generation on the supplied connection and returns its result projection for the enclosing receipt transaction.
limits: Enclosing mutate_runtime_session stores its exact-retry receipt on the same connection; no universal legacy-writer claim.

statement: Hermes home resolves context-local override before environment and platform default; named profile state must retain that identity through child work.
limits: Profile configuration isolation is not an OS security boundary or an audited medical data-access policy.

statement: Delegate child construction makes fresh isolated conversation with supplied goal/context, derived depth role, skipped project/default memory and a fresh iteration budget.
limits: skip_memory exception for explicit memory toolsets exists in init; child context/terminal session isolation does not imply separate filesystem or tenant sandbox.

statement: Delegation defaults are250 iterations per child,24,000 summary characters, no child idle timeout,10 concurrent children and inherited MCP toolsets.
limits: Operator overrides apply; dynamic parent-headroom limit also bounds summaries, and actual supported child tools are filtered separately.

statement: Delegate max_iterations argument from caller is ignored when it differs from authoritative delegation configuration.
limits: No shared-parent-budget inference; aggregate spend across independently budgeted children still needs policy.

statement: Public lifecycle API documents capability handles, cooperative cancel, immutable bounded result/hash and unavailable reconnect after process restart.
limits: Documentation contract inspected, not full API exercise; Python threads do not survive host exit.

statement: Skills use progressive disclosure: lightweight index/list and full skill_view content plus support files.
limits: A selected skill can still load substantial content; its mere presence does not prove correct procedural learning.

statement: Default skill writes need no approval; inline shell snippets are off; agent-created guard off; ledger on with5MiB cap; project discovery requires trusted root.
limits: Hub install scanning and operator trust are distinct; a ledger is provenance/rollback support, not validation of skill correctness.

statement: Curator defaults enabled, weekly interval,2h idle,14day stale,30day archive, LLM consolidation off, built-in prune off and backup keep2.
limits: Defaults describe maintenance policy, not measured learning; archive TTL default0 and explicit purge differ from automatic deletion.

statement: Post-turn finalizer can spawn a background memory/skill review only when due, noninterrupted, final response exists and background review not skipped.
limits: Not every turn forks. General plugin on_session_end hook is called here but memory-provider session-end cleanup is explicitly elsewhere.

statement: Background review defaults enabled unless finite-turn or safe-worker policy suppresses it; config-read failure leaves review enabled with warning.
limits: This is fail-open for optional learning behavior/cost, not a security recommendation; no review-model calls were executed.

statement: Cron constructs agents with skip_memory=False, load_soul_identity=True and skip_background_review=True; project context depends on configured workdir.
limits: Contradicts stale agent AGENTS.md cron skip_memory=True claim; actual selected toolsets and provider gates still apply.

statement: Security policy treats OS-level whole-process isolation as containment and distinguishes it from terminal-backend sandbox and in-process heuristic checks.
limits: Published trust model, not penetration-test result or security certification. No sandbox/runtime was launched.

statement: Approval default is smart, while cron/single-query/unattended modes default deny.
limits: Actual guard participation depends on tool path/config; not all possible host effects are thereby contained.

statement: Approval module has per-session state and a default three-consecutive-smart-denial breaker; frozen launch YOLO state cannot be changed by a later environment read.
limits: An in-process heuristic, not a sandbox; user-configured bypass/floors have separate semantics.

statement: Plugin architecture documents different discovery precedence for general, memory and model-provider plugins; context engines are separate kind-specific extensions.
limits: Documentation design contract inspected; installer/package compatibility and all plugin execution isolation paths not audited.

statement: Context-engine selection documentation requires explicit config and falls back to built-in compressor; engines are not activated simply because installed.
limits: Plugin implementation such as LCM not audited here; fallback and selection wiring statically inspected in agent_init1904 onward.

statement: Gateway health monitoring defaults off and OTLP export off; typed events are intended content-free operational health/diagnostics rather than transcript export.
limits: Separate logs, usage auditing, traces and plugin telemetry may carry different content and retention; no global privacy guarantee.

statement: Upstream test contracts inspect frozen memory snapshots, roundtrip storage and oversized file loading.
limits: Tests inspected only, not executed; selected range covers roundtrip/oversize/frozen snapshot, not all test claims elsewhere.

statement: Usage-anchor tests explicitly exercise prefix rewrites preserving the final priced row and matching reloaded transcript content.
limits: Tests inspected, not executed; no vendor-tokenizer comparison.

statement: Runtime admission tests cover durable request identity/conflict and claim/recovery behavior.
limits: Tests inspected, not executed. Assertions are evidence of intended contract, not measured production reliability.

statement: Gateway hygiene documentation describes separate85% safety threshold using prior real usage, persisted anchor then rough fallback.
limits: Docs-only here: actual gateway/run_turn_hygiene.py is additional implementation to audit for changed guards; built-in main compressor does not always fire at50%.

statement: Compression guide explains failed-summary cooldowns, deterministic degradation, overload escalation and manual/provider-overflow bypasses.
limits: Documentation-only detailed failure ladder; core compress/overflow call path traced but every failure class not dynamically tested.

statement: MemoryProvider ABC exposes prefetch, sync_turn, session lifecycle, pre-compress checkpoint and memory-write notification seams.
limits: An interface contract does not prove provider-specific privacy, deletion, embeddings or durable implementation.

statement: Session-storage guide describes canonical gateway ownership, separate runtime workers and archive generations rather than treating all clients as independent transcript writers.
limits: Architecture documentation; direct AIAgent/batch/legacy modes have scope caveats, so not every process universally gateway-only.
